sights.w: Jōdo temple where Tokugawa Ieyasu headquartered during the Sieges of Osaka; famous for its okotsu-butsu Buddhas moulded from the ashes of the dead and accepting remains regardless of sect.

sights.n: Abe no Seimei Shrine (安倍晴明神社)
sights.w: Shrine on the reputed birthplace of the Heian onmyōji Abe no Seimei, with his statue and 'birth-bath' well; an outlying shrine of Abe Ōji Jinja.
Osaka's 'Ebessan', packed by about a million merchants each 9–11 January for Tōka Ebisu lucky-bamboo; first stop on the Osaka Seven Lucky Gods pilgrimage.

sights.address: Jan Jan Yokochō, Ebisuhigashi, Naniwa-ku, Osaka
sights.w: Showa-era smartball parlour in Jan Jan Yokochō — Osaka's only hall dedicated entirely to smartball, running 50+ years.
